utterances.text: Good morning. What brings you in today?
Doctor, I've been having this terrible pain after I eat for about two weeks now. It's like a burning feeling right here in my upper stomach. Sometimes it wakes me up at night too.
I see. Any nausea or vomiting? Have you noticed any blood in your stool?
No vomiting, but I do feel nauseous sometimes. No blood that I've noticed. I've also been taking ibuprofen almost every day for the past six months for my back pain.
Are you on any other medications? Any allergies?

Yes, I take Zestril for my blood pressure, 10 milligrams daily. And omeprizole 20 milligrams but I ran out last month. No allergies to any medications. I don't smoke but I do have two drinks on weekends.

Let me examine you. Blood pressure is 134 over 82. Heart rate 78, regular. Abdomen is soft but there is tenderness in the epigastric area. No rebound. No guarding. Bowel sounds are normal. I don't feel any masses.

Based on your symptoms, the burning pain after eating, the nocturnal awakening, and especially the daily ibuprofen use for six months, I'm concerned about peptic ulcer disease or possibly GERD. I'd like to start you back on omeprazole 20 milligrams daily and we need to stop the ibuprofen. Let's also check an H. pylori stool antigen test. I want to see you back in four weeks. If the pain gets worse or you notice any blood, please come to the emergency room right away.

patient_summary_en.assessment_summary: Based on your symptoms (stomach pain after eating, burning sensation, and night-time discomfort) along with your regular use of ibuprofen, your doctor suspects you may have a stomach ulcer or acid reflux (GERD). These conditions are treatable with the right medication and lifestyle changes.
patient_summary_en.plan_summary:
Your doctor has made the following plan:
• Start taking omeprazole 20 mg once daily (this helps reduce stomach acid)
• Stop taking ibuprofen (it can irritate your stomach lining)
• Get an H. pylori test (a stool test to check for a stomach bacteria)
• Come back for a follow-up visit in 4 weeks
medications_list: Omeprazole 20 mg — Take once daily before breakfast
Lisinopril 10 mg — Continue taking daily for blood pressure
STOP ibuprofen — Do not take until your doctor says it's safe
🧬 omeprazole — Personalized dosing recommended based on your CYP2C19 genetic profile (responder)
red_flag_warnings: 🚨 Go to the Emergency Room IMMEDIATELY if you experience:
• Severe or sudden worsening of stomach pain
• Blood in your stool (dark or tarry stools)
• Vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds
• Feeling faint, dizzy, or extremely weak

⚠️ Genetic Alert for omeprazole: Your genetic test shows a intermediate_metabolizer profile (CYP2C19). Your doctor may adjust the dose to 43.9 mg/day [0.0, 94.0] 90% CI. Monitoring: Standard monitoring. Assess for PPI-related side effects (headache, diarrhea) if prolonged use.
